submission.natural_language_explanation: Layer-0 head whose strength is how far its attention-weighted average of the values of the tokens read so far sits from its corpus-mean write; in a text's first two or three positions it attends almost wholly to a single token (itself, or the first token), so what fires it is that token's value - the English articles ' the', ' a', ' an' (0.6-1.0 of max at position 1, about half that by positions 4-6, and 0.1-0.4 of max after position 8, so a late article can still sit near the line), an attached comma (0.8-0.9 at positions 1-2, about 0.6 at position 6, about 0.3 by positions 12-20) and content words or word pieces at positions 1-2 (0.4-1.0) - while at position 1 'this', 'that', 'these', 'my', 'every', 'each', 'no', 'one', 'two', ' and', ' of', ' from', ' by', ' at', ' in', ' on' and ' or' reach only 0-0.2 of max (' to', ' for', ' with' and ' were' reach 0.3-0.4). Ordinary prose, names, TeX/SQL and most code are predicted active-weak: their peak is usually 0.25-0.6 of max, at a determiner, a content word or word piece near the start, a content word that the next token copies (e.g. 'music played') or a sentence-final full stop - nearly every sentence containing an article or comma clears the 0.25 line, while about half of short determiner-free sentences fall just below it; predicted inactive (0.01-0.21 of max, never above the line) are short strings built only of the single-token particles, adverbs and prepositions 'up, down, in, out, on, off, over, under, back, forth, round, about, through, to, fro, by, from, of, and, again' joined by ' and', ' of', ' from' or ' by', with no article, content noun, number or comma ('Up and down', 'In and out', 'Back and forth', 'On and on', 'Over and over', 'Through and through', 'Up and down and in and out', 'On and on and on and on'), which a comma or an article-plus-noun after the chain usually ends and activates ('Up and down the street' 0.58, 'Up and down, up and down' 0.44), while bare repetitions of one particle with no connective ('up up up up', 0.4) are outside the class.

rival_explanations: Only the English articles ' the', ' a', ' an' and an attached comma within a text's first three tokens fire this head; ordinary prose, content words and word pieces never clear the line.
The head is a position detector: any token at positions 1-2 of a text fires it whatever it is, and it is silent once a text is past its opening, so token identity does not matter.
The head marks clause and phrase boundaries: a comma anywhere, or a determiner opening a new phrase, is active with little or no dependence on how far into the text it sits.
